 "We created a lot of chances. Disappointing to lose. Didn't manage to put chances away, on another day we put three or four away, We have to bounce back for the Champions League game in a couple of days.

 Palace proving too easy to breach published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Tottenham away used to be a trip of trepidation across London for Crystal Palace fans but the tide has certainly turned in recent years.
 After nine straight top-flight losses at Spurs they have won on their last two visits, with their 3-1 victory in March particularly impressive.
 However, this is a Palace team in a very different spot. Defeat to Newcastle on Sunday was their fifth in just eight league matches under new boss Pierre Sage.
 They sit 17th having conceded a top-flight high of 19 goals in eight matches, the second most they have let in at this stage of a top-flight season after 22 in 1980-81.
 Of the 24 previous Premier League teams to concede 19 after eight games, 14 went on to be relegated. And another concerning stat is that they have let in at least two goals in 12 of their last 14 top-flight games.
 These defensive frailties, though, can't all be put at Sage's feet as they predate the Frenchman's summer arrival. Their tally of conceding 50 goals in 2026 is not only a Premier League high, but it's also six more than they conceded in the whole of 2025 and they still have 10 league matches to play this year.

Former Liverpool midfielder on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 On whether he would play Lisandro Martinez again...
 No, I wouldn't, only because he looks like he has already gone. 
 His head isn't right. He is not going to be there long term, that is evident.
 You have to put the club first. Michael has got to make some big decisions. You can't have a liability in your team.
 People talked about Romero for years, and it is turning into that a little bit. That petulance, that behaviour on the pitch is not acceptable.
 He has been poor for a while and he has had injury problems. He is not the answer.

 'Amount of bodies on the line today was incredible' published at 17:12 GMT 17:12 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen speaking to Sky Sports: "Unbelievable feeling. We go 1-0 up and then to hang tight the last 30-40 minutes we completely lost control of the game. The manager said this morning we have to dig deep and that's what we did. So happy to get over the line and can't wait to celebrate with the boys."
 On if Brighton are in the title race: "We are on game nine so not really. We'll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what's ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things."
 On keeping a clean sheet: "Hard to point out one thing, the mentality to keep the ball out of the net - how hard we work. The amount of bodies put on the line today is incredible and credit to all the boys and staff and how hard we worked to keep the clean sheets. Hopefully we can get many more."
 On if this was one of his best personal performances: "I don't know - it was a good game from all of us. Happy to help the team and make some important saves but I wasn't the only one. I think there were four or five shots blocked in an amazing way as well. Joint effort from everyone. We celebrate and go again."

BBC Sport chief football writer at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium 
 It will be something of a disappointment for Spurs fans that James Maddison is only on the bench after his sparkling return from injury, but there will also be a tinge of relief because there were fears he might face another lengthy lay-off when he went down injured during the win at Chelsea last Saturday.
 Head coach Roberto De Zerbi offered assurances that his groin problem was not serious, and so it has proved as he is named on the bench for the home game against Crystal Palace.

 By Chris McKenna BBC Sport journalist Frank Lampard's Coventry City have lifted themselves out of relegation zone by beating struggling Sunderland, who remain rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table. 
 Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni scored to secure the Sky Blues just their third league win of the season, meaning Enzo Le Fee's second-half penalty was a mere consolation for the out-of-form Black Cats.
 Both sides came into the game occupying the bottom two places in the table with just six goals scored each.
 Coventry boss Lampard made four changes from last weekend's defeat by Fulham , including dropping captain Matt Grimes, and it stirred a positive performance from his side.
 They were helped by some poor defending from Sunderland as the Black Cats made a mess of a routine cross that saw the ball fall to Sakamoto, and he opened the scoring with a fine finish in the 17th minute from the edge of the area.
 Awoniyi then nicked the ball off Sunderland's Luke O'Nien far too easily in the 37th minute before he scored via a deflection after coasting through the visitors' defence and past some weak challenges.
 Other than a decent opportunity for Brian Brobbey, which he fired wide, Sunderland were ineffective at the other end in the first half.
 Their chances of getting back into the game were realistically ended just seven minutes into the second half when Rudoni's shot deflected off Omar Alderete, who had stuck out a leg to try to block it, and it found the net.
 Sunderland's Chemsdine Talbi missed a good chance before the visitors were awarded a penalty after referee Simon Hooper took an age to review a handball by Coventry defender Ethan Pinnock, whose arm was up to block O'Nien's shot.
 Le Fee scored the resulting spot-kick in the 67th minute, but there would be no stirring comeback from the Black Cats as they suffered their sixth defeat in nine league games.
 Their misery was compounded by Alderete getting sent off in stoppage time for a second bookable offence when he tripped Rudoni.
 Coventry analysis: Lampard's team selection pays off 
 After disappointing defeats by Tottenham and Fulham, Lampard made a bold decision to make four changes including moving his captain to the bench.
 He also restored summer signing Awoniyi to the starting line-up for the first time since he was sent off in a 5-0 defeat by Brighton on 13 September.
 The changes helped restore some energy to the Sky Blues, but they were also clinical as they scored three goals from four shots on target and an XG of just 0.71.
 Two of the goals also had a touch of fortune given that deflections helped take them beyond Sunderland keeper Robin Roefs.
 But it was a huge win for Lampard and his side against fellow strugglers, and the manager's team-selection was backed up with an important three points.
 Coventry have lost as many games as Sunderland but, crucially, they have three victories under their belt.
 What did you learn from Coventry’s display? 
 Sunderland analysis: Defensive woes continue for sloppy Black Cats 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sunderland have struggled defensively this season
 Last season, Sunderland were renowned for being a well-drilled and organised side, with only Arsenal, Manchester City and Brighton conceding fewer goals.
 But Regis le Bris' side have now let in 17 goals in just nine games in this campaign.
 That helps explain why they have won just a single league game so far - against Fulham on 30 August.
 They definitely miss Dan Ballard in their back line, with the defender out since late September due to a hamstring injury.
 But they continually make errors, as proven here with Coventry's first two goals - and centre-back Alderete will now be suspended for next week's clash with Chelsea.
 They did at least show some more attacking threat here with 17 attempts on goal and more possession that their opponents, but it was not nearly enough.
